artists.biography: Anneke van Giersbergen (born March 8, 1973) was the singer in the Dutch band The Gathering from 1995 to 2007 when she announced her departure, summer 2007. She has since formed Agua de Annique with whom she released new songs in the fall of 2007. She has also worked with Devin Townsend Project, Danny Cavanagh & Anathema, Lawn, The Farmer Boys , Ayreon, Napalm Death, Globus, Moonspell, Giant Squid, Novembers Doom, Wetton/Downes, Maiden United and she has also done a live guest performance for Within Temptation. Her new album "The Darkest Skies Are The Brightest" is out now. Dianne van Giersbergen and Anneke van Giersbergen are both Dutch symphonic metal singers with the same last name. They are not related, but share a common last name, which is also the name of a small village in the Netherlands. They are both known for their strong vocal abilities and have achieved notable success in the symphonic metal scene. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Pure Air is a 2009 compilation album by Anneke van Giersbergen with her band Agua de Annique, released on Agua Recordings. The album blends rock, pop, and progressive elements, showcasing Anneke’s versatile voice and the band’s dynamic musical approach. It features a mix of original tracks and covers, including notable collaborations with artists such as Danny Cavanagh (Anathema), Arjen Lucassen (Ayreon), John Wetton (King Crimson, Asia), and Sharon den Adel (Within Temptation). The musical style ranges from atmospheric and melodic rock to more experimental and emotionally charged arrangements, highlighting Anneke’s ability to navigate different moods and genres within a single release.

Pure Air serves as a bridge between Anneke’s earlier work with Agua de Annique and her subsequent solo career, capturing the creative energy of her post-The Gathering years. The album draws tracks from the band’s debut Air (2007) and adds new material and guest performances, making it both a retrospective and a statement of artistic evolution. While not a commercial blockbuster, Pure Air was well-received by critics and fans for its strong songwriting, emotional depth, and the quality of its collaborations. It remains a significant release in Anneke van Giersbergen’s discography, illustrating her transition from gothic metal frontwoman to a more diverse and mature rock artist.
